# Scholarly Infrastructure · 大师荟萃之楼

A batteries-included Python toolkit that helps ML/AI researchers run reproducible experiments, tune hyperparameters, and log results without rewriting boilerplate.

<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

> “所谓大学者，非谓有大楼之谓也，有大师之谓也。” ——梅贻琦
>
> “A first-class university is not top for its grand infrastructures, but by its great scholars.” —— Mei Yiqi

Scholarly Infrastructure turns Mei Yiqi's insight into engineering practice: great research is built on great *infrastructure*, not just one-off scripts. It is an open-source Python library that lets any ML/AI researcher manage experiment arguments, hyperparameter optimization, logging, and LLM access in a reproducible, composable way.

## Introduction

**Scholarly Infrastructure** is a modular Python toolkit for machine-learning and AI research. Instead of re-implementing argument parsing, hyperparameter search, logging, and config loading for every project, you compose a small set of well-tested building blocks:

- declare experiment arguments once and reuse them as configs, command-line flags, and Optuna search spaces;
- turn an ordinary config-driven training script into a distributed hyperparameter study with a single command;
- log rich, ML-aware output — including PyTorch model structure and parameter summaries;
- call LLMs through one unified interface.

It is built with [`nbdev`](https://nbdev.fast.ai), so the documentation *is* the source code and every API ships with runnable notebooks.

## Key Features

- **`rv_args` — Arguments as Random Variables.** Define hyperparameters and configs as typed dataclass fields and automatically derive an Optuna search space (`get_optuna_search_space`) and an `argparse` interface (`argparse_parser_add_arguments`). Reproducible, Bayesian-ready configuration with zero boilerplate.
- **`experiment.auto_optuna` — Zero-code-change HPO.** Wrap any config-driven research script into an Optuna study with `tune` (CMA-ES + Hyperband pruning) and `ablation` (grid search, fully reproducible) modes — no need to rewrite your training loop.
- **`logging` — Rich, ML-aware logging.** `richuru`-powered console output plus a `torch` helper that inspects model structure and parameter counts at a glance.
- **`llm_api` — Unified LLM access.** A single interface for calling LLMs inside research and data-processing pipelines.
- **`nbscholar` — `nbdev` workflow helpers.** `separate` / `export` / `check` commands that keep notebook-as-source development clean and reviewable.

## Modules at a Glance

- **`rv_args`** — Declare experiment arguments and hyperparameters as typed dataclass fields ("random variables"); automatically derive Optuna search spaces (`get_optuna_search_space`) and `argparse` interfaces (`argparse_parser_add_arguments`). See [`01_rv_args.ipynb`](https://github.com/THU-CVML/ScholarlyInfrastructure/blob/main/src/notebooks/01_rv_args%20%28arguments%20are%20random%20variables%29.ipynb).
- **`experiment`** — `auto_optuna` wraps any config-driven research script into an Optuna study, with `tune` (CMA-ES + Hyperband pruning) and `ablation` (grid search, reproducible) modes. See [`01_experiment.ipynb`](https://github.com/THU-CVML/ScholarlyInfrastructure/blob/main/src/notebooks/01_experiment%20%28parameters%20management%29.ipynb).
- **`logging`** — `richuru`-based rich logging; the `torch` helper inspects model structure and parameter counts at a glance. See [`02_logging.ipynb`](https://github.com/THU-CVML/ScholarlyInfrastructure/blob/main/src/notebooks/02_logging%20%28richuru%29.ipynb) and [`02a_torch.ipynb`](https://github.com/THU-CVML/ScholarlyInfrastructure/blob/main/src/notebooks/02a_torch%20%28inspect%20torch%20model%29.ipynb).
- **`llm_api`** — A single interface for calling LLMs inside research and data pipelines. See [`04_llm_api.ipynb`](https://github.com/THU-CVML/ScholarlyInfrastructure/blob/main/src/notebooks/04_llm_api.ipynb).
- **`nbscholar`** — `nbdev` workflow helpers (`separate` / `export` / `check`) that keep notebook-as-source development clean. See [`03_nbscholar.ipynb`](https://github.com/THU-CVML/ScholarlyInfrastructure/blob/main/src/notebooks/03_nbscholar%20%28nbdev%20extensions%29.ipynb).
- **`nucleus` / `help`** — Core infrastructure and the library overview. See [`00_help.ipynb`](https://github.com/THU-CVML/ScholarlyInfrastructure/blob/main/src/notebooks/00_help%20%28library%20information%29.ipynb).

## Installation

Install from the GitHub [repository][repo]:

```sh
$ pip install git+https://github.com/THU-CVML/ScholarlyInfrastructure.git
```

or from [pypi][pypi] (published on PyPI):

```sh
$ pip install scholarly_infrastructure
```

Requires Python >= 3.7.

[repo]: https://github.com/THU-CVML/ScholarlyInfrastructure
[pypi]: https://pypi.org/project/scholarly_infrastructure/

## 📖 **Usage**

### Documentation

Full, runnable documentation lives in the [`src/notebooks/`](https://github.com/THU-CVML/ScholarlyInfrastructure/tree/main/src/notebooks) directory (rendered with nbdev). Start with `00_help.ipynb` for the library overview, then `01_rv_args.ipynb` (arguments as random variables) and `01_experiment.ipynb` (auto Optuna).

### Quick Start

```python
import scholarly_infrastructure as si

# The library is organized into composable, lazily-imported submodules:
si.rv_args     # arguments as random variables + Optuna / argparse bridges
si.experiment  # auto_optuna: turn config-driven runs into Optuna studies
si.logging     # rich, ML-aware logging (incl. PyTorch model inspection)
si.llm_api     # unified LLM access
si.nbscholar   # nbdev workflow helpers
```

# Turn a config-driven training script into an Optuna study:
#     si.experiment.auto_optuna(mode="tune")      # CMA-ES + Hyperband
#     si.experiment.auto_optuna(mode="ablation")  # grid search, reproducible

See `src/notebooks/01_rv_args.ipynb` and `01_experiment.ipynb` for complete, runnable examples.

## 🤝 **Contributing**

Contributions are welcome! Here's how you can quickly get involved. Please review our [contribution guidelines](CONTRIBUTING.md) for more details. 

### git guide

1. Fork the repository and then git clone it to your local machine: `git clone https://github.com/your-username/ScholarlyInfrastructure.git`.  
2. Create a new branch for your feature or bug fix: `git checkout -b feature-name`.  
3. Commit your changes: `git commit -m "Add feature-name"`.  
4. Push your branch: `git push origin feature-name`.  
5. Open a pull request and describe your changes.  



---

### nbdev framework guide

Our project utilizes `nbdev` to manage our codes, tests and documentation.
If you are new to using `nbdev` here are some quick points to get you started.

#### 1. Install this libary in Development mode

After you have cloned the repository, and before you start working on it, you need to pip install this library in development mode. This can be done using the following command:

```sh
# make sure NamableClassify package is installed in development mode
$ pip install -e .[dev]
```

#### 2. make changes under `notebooks/` directory

use `#| export` for exported codes.  

#### 3. check and synchronize before git commit 

```sh
# compile to have changes apply to the python module
$ nbdev_prepare
```
